post.description: Run a query object (F-8.9); the result carries its query and provenance.

Count the features of several queries at once, e.g. one per condition (design B2).

Nothing but numbers leaves the server. A rejected query names its position
in ``details.index``. All of them share one time limit, as one query would:
a request of many slow counts must not hold a worker many times as long.

The ids of the features a query returns, for marking hits (design B9).

No geometry or attribute is sent, so the result-size limit does not apply.
Check a query against schema and data core without running it (F-5.9).

get.description: The versioned query-object JSON schema (F-10.3).

schema.title: Response Query Object Schema Api Schema Query Object Get

get.description: The data catalog (design D2).

schema.title: Response Layers Api Admin Layers Get

patch.description: Rename (title only, the identifier stays) and describe a layer (F-2.7, F-2.8).

delete.description: Delete a layer and its data for good (F-2.7; no archive, plan D2).

post.description: A copy of a layer: data, metadata and visibility (design D2), logged like an import.

get.description: The layer profile as the model will see it (F-2.9); ``null`` if not for the model.

schema.title: Response Layer Profile Api Admin Layers  Name  Profile Get

post.description: Step 1: stage the file and preview it with detected options (F-2.4).
Read again with other options: encoding, delimiter, sheet or layer (design D11).

Import with the wizard's decisions. The outcome, also a failed one, is in ``status``.

A successful import removes the staged file; after a failed one it stays,
so the decisions can be corrected and committed again.

delete.description: Close the wizard without importing; logged as aborted (design D7).

schema.title: Response Import Runs Api Admin Import Log Get
Response Users Api Admin Users Get

patch.description: Change role, lock or unlock, rename; never the last active administrator away.

get.description: Layer by role; administrators always see every layer. New imports start hidden.

schema.title: Response Visibility Matrix Api Admin Visibility Get
Response Set Visibility Api Admin Visibility Put

get.description: Every connection; the API key never leaves, ``has_api_key`` says whether one is set.

schema.title: Response Llm Connections Api Admin Llm Connections Get

post.description: Test before saving; the result is not kept. Always 200: failures are steps.
Test a saved connection and keep the result with it (C12).

get.description:
The layer profile a model would get for ``account``: only what that account
sees and the administrator released for the model (F-9.3, F-5.10), sized
against the context length of the connection it would use (S5).

post.description:
Create the first administrator; closed as soon as any account exists.

Only with the installation's token: reaching the address is not enough
(security review #1). Wrong tokens are braked like failed sign-ins.
Repeated failures are braked per username and client address (review #2).

A changed password signs out every other login, e.g. one with a stolen cookie.

Wrong current passwords count like failed sign-ins: a stolen cookie must
not become a way to guess the password (review #2).

schema.title: Response List Sessions Api Sessions Get

post.description: Save the analysis as a new session ("Speichern unter", design C2).

get.description: The session to open after sign-in; null when there is none (design A2).

schema.title: Response Last Api Sessions Last Get

put.description: Overwrite with the current state ("Speichern"); sets a new stamp.

post.description:
Open with check (design C4): the saved query again, against the saved stamp.

With the query the interface rebuilt from the saved state, also tells
whether state and query still agree (``state_matches``).

schema.title: Response List Queries Api Queries Get

put.description:
Choose a connection, a level or both. A disabled connection is refused for
administrators too (C14); a level users may not choose is refused for users.
The person's choice only (``session_required`` for a token, WP71): a program
acting for the account must not move it to a level without approval.

post.description:
Ask the model (F-5.1). Level and connection are the account's, resolved
here (H6, C17). Stores the action record and answers at once with it,
``thinking``; the client polls ``GET /actions/{id}`` and may abort. No
result data: an ``auto`` answer arrives ``approved`` and the client
executes it (D2); one with an ``off`` class is a proposal the user applies
by hand (D1). Closes the account's open record (WP70). One prompt of an
account at a time (409 ``busy``); all model calls at once are bounded
(503 ``busy``).

get.description:
One own record, or any for an administrator (D4); polled while the model
thinks (P7) and while a chain runs (P4).

post.description:
Count, the result layer's total and ids of the stored query, for the user
only (P2): an interactive session (``session_required`` for any token), no
class ``off`` (``class_not_allowed``), status unchanged. A ``POST``: it
writes ``previewed_at``, so it is a change the origin check covers (review
#39).

Refused with ``class_not_allowed`` when a class is ``off`` at the level as
it was (D1, D2, M7.3); only ``proposed``.
Only ``proposed``; with the optional reason chip (design M5.3).

Run the stored query, never a sent one (the route takes no body); only
``approved``, by the user or by an ``auto`` cell (D2): else ``not_approved``,
and ``already_decided`` once it ran. The one answer with rows.

For the log: the client restores the analysis itself (D2). Only the
account's last change made by the model, and ``undo_blocked`` once a hand
edit after it was reported (``touched``).

The analysis was changed by hand after this applied action: undo is over
(design rule 7). Reporting it again changes nothing.

While thinking: ``aborted``; the model's late answer is dropped. A running
chain stops before its next step and becomes ``limited`` with its last
complete result adoptable (P4, WP75).

patch.description:
Change values and remove steps of a chain that waits for approval and has
not started; never add one (design M8.3). The plan is checked whole again
and governed by the level as it was; 422 names the step a refusal is
about. The person's edit: an interactive session only, as ``approve``.

post.description:
Start an ``approved`` chain, or let it go on after a halt (P4): 202 with
the record ``running``; the client polls ``GET /actions/{id}``. The steps
run one at a time as the caller's background task, among the model calls
(409/503 ``busy``); the record halts for approval where the level as it
was asks for it.

A ``done`` or ``limited`` chain's result becomes the analysis (design
"Kette übernehmen"): its last complete step as one query object, run as
the caller like ``execute``; the other answer with rows. Once only. The
person's decision (``accepted``): an interactive session only.

Ask again with the other approach (design M10.1): a new action with
``compare_of``, polled like any other. A prompt, so as ``/prompt``: the
account's level and connection now, its request limit, one at a time
(409/503 ``busy``). Only an own record with a result to compare, never a
repeat (``repeat_of_repeat``); it stays open beside the repeat, which
waits ``proposed`` whatever the level.

Once both have a result (else 409): both stamps and the difference by
feature ids, with names (design M10.2, M10.3), computed from both stored
queries run as the caller; the model is not asked. Feature ids and names
for the person, as the preview's ids (P2): an interactive session only,
and a side that waits gets ``previewed_at``; so a ``POST``, a change the
origin check covers, as the preview (review #41). The reason is data (which
layer, which conditions), worded by the interface. Addressed by either
side: the repeat, or the record compared (its newest repeat with a
result). 409 ``not_approved`` while a side may still get a result,
``nothing_to_compare`` once it ended without one.

get.description:
The account's own entries, newest first (D4, design M16.3); an
administrator's too, the log of all is ``/api/admin/model-actions``.
Newest first, every account's; ``total`` counts all that match.
Plan section 2, computed over the action table for the filters.

CSV of the filtered log, prompt text included (D4); cells safe against
formula injection (``model/record/export.py`` names the columns). Streamed
a row at a time; more than ``MAX_EXPORT_ROWS`` rows are refused (413).

Any account's record as it was (design M16.2), a failure's technical
details included (D4); 404 when there is none.

The start set and the own cases, start cases first (V1.1); each with its
status (D3), ``invalid`` by the checks alone. The list leaves
``reference_hits`` out.

post.description:
An own case: authored in the workplace (V3), taken from the log (V2 from
M16.2) or copied from a start case. Its reference passes the checks a model
query passes (``case_invalid``); an id in use is ``case_id_taken``.

get.description:
The own cases as a case file (F-3.13, F-10.4); with ``start`` the start set
too, and then without an own case behind a start id (logged). Without
``null`` fields, so export and import are a round trip.

post.description: All or nothing (V1.3): one invalid case and none is taken.

get.description:
A case prefilled from a logged direct query with decision ``accepted``, or
``auto`` not undone (F-3.14); nothing is stored until it is saved with
``POST /cases``. Any other action, a hand-corrected one too (decision 2), is
``action_not_eligible``.
One case with the hits of its reference on its data state (V2.1).

put.description:
A start case is ``case_read_only``; editing a stale or invalid case makes
it run again. An own case behind a start id (a later start set brought it)
is reached here, so it can be renamed.

delete.description: A start case is ``case_read_only``; an own case behind a start id is deleted.

post.description:
Requests, tokens, cost and duration before the start (D12, V4.1); no
model call. A selection without a runnable case is ``no_cases``, as at the
start.

Starts the run in the background and answers at once, ``running``; the
client polls ``GET /runs/{id}`` (D8). One run at a time (``run_busy``); an
external connection not in ``confirm_external``, or whose host is not in
``confirm_external_hosts`` (changed since the estimate), is
``external_not_confirmed``;
a selection with no runnable case (all filtered out, stale or invalid) is
refused before the start, 400 ``no_cases``. ``RunView.error`` is for what
fails while the run runs.

get.description: Newest first; with ``connection_id`` the runs that measured it (O7).
Polled while the run runs; figures and comparisons once it is done.

post.description: Stops before the next question; the answers so far stay.

get.description: The repeats of one case at one measuring point (V7).

schema.title: Response Answers Api Admin Evaluation Runs  Run Id  Answers Get

get.description:
The run with every answer, as JSON (V6.2 *Exportieren*): written as it is
read, the answers a batch at a time, so a large run is never held whole
(security review #46). Every key of the schema is present, ``null`` ones
too.

post.description:
Two complete runs over the same cases side by side (V6.6, D7);
otherwise ``runs_not_comparable``.

get.description:
How complete the metadata is that the model sees (D11, V8): of the sample
data, or of the live catalog as ``account`` sees it (default: the caller).
An unknown ``account`` is 404, as on ``GET /api/admin/llm/profile``; the
sample is the same for every account (D4).

ActionPreview.title: ActionPreview
ActionPreview.description: The user's preview before approval (P2): never shown to the model.

area_fields.title: Area Fields
area_fields.description: Attributes of ``by_layer`` kept in the result.

Aggregate.title: Aggregate
Aggregate.description:
Summarise source features per feature of an area layer (F-4.7).

Every area feature appears in the result, with ``count`` 0 and other
metrics null where no source feature relates to it.

AnswerView.title: AnswerView

condition.title: Condition
condition.description: Path of indexes into the query's where tree; lets 'ändern' open it.

Assumption.title: Assumption
Assumption.description: One assumption, shown with ≈ (F-5.12, design M2, M12.1).

AttributeJoin.title: AttributeJoin
AttributeJoin.description:
Left join of a layer by key (F-4.6).

Joined fields are addressable by their name, or by ``prefix + name`` when a
prefix is given; clashes with source attributes are rejected.

bbox.title: Bbox
bbox.description: Two opposite corners [lon, lat, lon, lat] in WGS84; stored as [min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat].

BBox.title: BBox
BBox.description: Source geometry intersects a WGS84 bounding box, e.g. the map view (F-4.3).

Between.title: Between
Between.description: Inclusive value range (F-4.2). The bounds may come in either order.

Buffer.title: Buffer
Buffer.description: Replace each source geometry by its buffer (F-4.5).

CannotAnswer.title: CannotAnswer
CannotAnswer.description:
Nothing to propose (design M13). With ``other_approach`` the answer offers
to try the other way of working (D6); without, it says what is missing.

CaseDraft.title: CaseDraft
CaseDraft.description:
A case not yet saved (V2 prefilled from M16.2, V3): no id and no tags yet;
the administrator adds them and saves it with ``POST /cases``.

CaseFile.title: CaseFile
CaseFile.description:
The start set, an export, an import: the same JSON (F-10.4), written
without ``null`` fields.

CaseLayer.title: CaseLayer
CaseLayer.description: A layer a live case uses, with its dataset version when the case was made (D3).

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: Optional fixed colour per category value.

Cell.title: Cell
Cell.description: One case at one measuring point: passes of the repeats and the rest's mix.

changed_layers.title: Changed Layers
changed_layers.description: Layers with a new dataset version.

missing_layers.title: Missing Layers
missing_layers.description: Layers deleted or no longer visible.

error.title: Error
error.description: Why the query no longer runs.

state_matches.title: State Matches
state_matches.description: The query rebuilt from the saved state is the saved query; null when none was sent.

Check.title: Check
Check.description: The saved stamp against the current data (design C4, C8).

rebuilt.description: The result query the interface rebuilt from the state.

has_result.title: Has Result
has_result.description: Whether the interface rebuilt a result at all.

Choice.title: Choice
Choice.description:
Only the fields sent change; ``null`` returns to the default. Nothing else
is accepted (422): a matrix, a level's cells or a connection's address sent
along would be ignored, but refusing them says so (WP71).

Clarification.title: Clarification
Clarification.description: Only when no sensible assumption exists (D5, design M12.2).

CompareRequest.title: CompareRequest
CompareRequest.description: Two complete runs over the same cases, side by side (V6.6, D7).

Comparison.title: Comparison
Comparison.description:
The two approaches side by side (design M10); the difference is the
application's, computed from feature ids, never the model's.

ConditionChange.title: ConditionChange
ConditionChange.description:
One condition the sides differ by: both about the same attribute or
layer, or ``None`` on the side that does not have it.

Conditions.title: Conditions
Conditions.description: Leaf conditions of the query, as design C6 shows them ("1 A · 2 R").

ConditionsReason.title: ConditionsReason
ConditionsReason.description: The sides differ by these top-level conditions, one by one.

reasoning_effort.title: Reasoning Effort
reasoning_effort.description: Unset: 'none' for a local connection, 'default' else (C10).

ConnectionDraft.title: ConnectionDraft
ConnectionDraft.description:
What the connection test needs, before or without saving (C12).

Editing a saved connection without retyping its key: name it in
``connection_id`` and the stored key is used, at its own address only.

ConnectionOption.title: ConnectionOption
ConnectionOption.description: What a user sees of a connection when choosing one (C7, C14).

ConnectionPatch.title: ConnectionPatch
ConnectionPatch.description: Only the fields sent change. ``api_key: null`` removes the key.

reasoning_effort.title: Reasoning Effort
reasoning_effort.description: Unset: 'none' for a local connection, 'default' else (C10).

may_receive_data.title: May Receive Data
may_receive_data.description: Unset: on for a local connection, off else (C6).

confirm_data_release.title: Confirm Data Release
confirm_data_release.description: Required to let an external connection receive data contents (C6).

request_limit_enabled.title: Request Limit Enabled
request_limit_enabled.description: Cap the requests per day, over all accounts (P5). Unset: off.

prompt_profile.description: How the direct query's prompt is written (plan E3, D9). Unset: today's.

price_currency.title: Price Currency
price_currency.description: With both prices or none of them (O4).

ConnectionWrite.title: ConnectionWrite
ConnectionWrite.description: A new connection (C4). Unset defaults follow from local or external.

CostEstimate.title: CostEstimate
CostEstimate.description:
What a run will ask before it starts (D12). Points run in one queue per
model host (D8): the connections of one host one after another, the hosts
at the same time, so ``duration_s`` is the longest of the hosts' sums.

CountMetric.title: CountMetric
CountMetric.description: Number of source features per area.

DecideRequest.title: DecideRequest
DecideRequest.description: The hand-over cases (P1, D2): applied by hand, or edited and applied via Modus A.

DiffEntry.title: DiffEntry
DiffEntry.description:
One difference of an answer's query to the reference (stage 1, D5): the
two condition nodes, never data.

DistanceColumn-Input.title: DistanceColumn
DistanceColumn-Input.description: Distance in metres to the nearest feature of ``layer``; null if none qualifies.

DistanceColumn-Output.title: DistanceColumn
DistanceColumn-Output.description: Distance in metres to the nearest feature of ``layer``; null if none qualifies.

DistanceRelation-Input.title: DistanceRelation
DistanceRelation-Input.description: Source within ``distance_m`` of a feature of ``layer``.

DistanceRelation-Output.title: DistanceRelation
DistanceRelation-Output.description: Source within ``distance_m`` of a feature of ``layer``.

EvalCase.title: EvalCase
EvalCase.description:
One question with its right answer (F-3.13, D2). Exactly one of ``gold``,
``gold_any``, ``require`` and ``expect``: a query case has a reference
query, several fair readings or required parts; a behaviour case names the
expected answer kind. A reference query is stored as the harness writes it,
without ``schema_version`` and ``output``, against ``schema_version``.

The JSON schema of the file cannot say "exactly one of"; the application
checks it, the uniqueness of ids and ``origin_action`` on import.

ExecuteResponse.title: ExecuteResponse
ExecuteResponse.description:
The only answer that carries rows: to the user, after ``execute`` or
``adopt`` (D2). The record keeps the stamp, not the features.

GeoJSONGeometry.title: GeoJSONGeometry
GeoJSONGeometry.description: GeoJSON geometry in WGS84. Coordinates are checked when compiled.

GeometryFilter.title: GeometryFilter
GeometryFilter.description: Source geometry relates to a drawn geometry (F-4.3).

Governance.title: Governance
Governance.description: What the level decides for this answer (H4, D1, design M6.3, M7.1).

Health.title: Health
Health.description:
For the container's health check and monitors: nothing else, as anyone may ask
(security review #10). Version, backend and capabilities are the administrators'
(``/api/admin/system``).

ImportDecisions.title: ImportDecisions
ImportDecisions.description: What the wizard settled (design D6); everything not given follows the preview.

ImportResult.title: ImportResult
ImportResult.description: All or nothing (V1.3): ``imported`` is 0 whenever ``problems`` is not empty.

IsNull.title: IsNull
IsNull.description: Attribute has no value. Combine with ``not`` for 'has a value'.

KeyFigures.title: KeyFigures
KeyFigures.description: Plan section 2, for the filters given (design M16.1).

LayerGaps.title: LayerGaps
LayerGaps.description:
What a layer lacks, in the order of care of Phase 4 (D11), with the totals
the shares of V8.1 are taken of.

LayerProfile.title: LayerProfile
LayerProfile.description:
What the model learns about a layer: structure and meaning, never content (F-9.3).

Metadata only (S1): nothing computed from the rows, so no feature count, no
extent, no distinct values. A value domain counts only once confirmed (S2).
Only layers and attributes marked ``for_model``.

LayerUpdate.title: LayerUpdate
LayerUpdate.description: Curated layer fields. ``name`` never changes; renaming sets ``title`` (plan D1).

Level.title: Level
Level.description: One level. In a set, the list order is the display order (H1).

LevelSet.title: LevelSet
LevelSet.description:
Every level in display order; saved as a whole, so its rules hold together (H7).
An unknown field, here or in a level, is refused (422): a misspelt
``selectable`` must not save a level with the default instead (WP71).

LevelSnapshot.title: LevelSnapshot
LevelSnapshot.description: The level as it was when the prompt was sent (H7, M7.3).

MeasuringPoint.title: MeasuringPoint
MeasuringPoint.description: A connection, its prompt profile and a level (D9, D10).

details.title: Details
details.description: Further values the message names, by key.

Message.title: Message
Message.description: A finding about the source; ``code`` is stable, ``message`` explains it.

ModelActionSummary.title: ModelActionSummary
ModelActionSummary.description: A row of the log (design M16.1, M16.3).

ModelActionView.title: ModelActionView
ModelActionView.description:
One action record as its owner or an administrator sees it (D4). Never
rows: those leave only in ``ExecuteResponse``.

ModelView.title: ModelView
ModelView.description:
What the model learns of a step (D9). Every field is a flag, a count, a
code or a name taken from the model's own query: nothing here can hold a
row, a geometry, an extent or an attribute value (D10).

NearFeature.title: NearFeature
NearFeature.description: Source geometry lies within a distance of one reference feature (F-4.3).

Op.title: Op
Op.description: Registered operations; each needs certain logical dialect functions (F-2.14).

OpClass.title: OpClass
OpClass.description:
What an operation does, fixed in code (H2). ``export`` joins with E5,
``external`` with E6; writes are no class, the model path has none (F-9.5).

PlanAnswer.title: PlanAnswer
PlanAnswer.description: A tool chain, planned in one call as structured output (P4).

PlanEdit.title: PlanEdit
PlanEdit.description: Change values or remove steps; never add one (design decision 17).

PointComparison.title: PointComparison
PointComparison.description:
One column against the reference column, paired per case (D7). Taken on
the ``confirm`` cases; ``None`` in a quick test or without them.

PointFigures.title: PointFigures
PointFigures.description:
Section 2 of the plan, for one measuring point; counts are answers (a
case counts once per repeat).

PointLabel.title: PointLabel
PointLabel.description: A measuring point as it was (H7): later edits change no run.

ProfileBudget.title: ProfileBudget
ProfileBudget.description:
The connection the account's model actions would use, and its declared
context length (C11, C17).

ProfileSummary.title: ProfileSummary
ProfileSummary.description: How complete the metadata the model sees is (D11, V8).

PromptProfile.title: PromptProfile
PromptProfile.description:
How the application writes the prompt for a connection (plan E3, D9):
measured presets, never free text. The default is today's prompt byte for
byte; P1, P2, P3, P4 and P8 are not offered (testplan-system-context 8.2).

PromptRequest.title: PromptRequest
PromptRequest.description: A prompt. No earlier turns: the server builds them from the parent chain (P6).

QueryObject-Input.title: GeoTandem query object
QueryObject-Input.description: Declarative, backend-neutral description of one analysis.

QueryObject-Output.title: GeoTandem query object
QueryObject-Output.description: Declarative, backend-neutral description of one analysis.

QueryResult.title: QueryResult
QueryResult.description: A GeoJSON FeatureCollection plus the query and its provenance.

QueueStop.title: QueueStop
QueueStop.description:
A model host whose queue tripped the circuit breaker: ``BREAKER_AFTER``
answers in a row with ``code``, after which the whole run stopped.

ReadOptions.title: ReadOptions
ReadOptions.description: How to read a file; every field is detected when left empty.

Require.title: Require
Require.description:
What a query must contain where several readings select different
features (harness ``require``): the source layer, and the conditions it
must hold.

RequiredCondition.title: RequiredCondition
RequiredCondition.description:
A condition the query must hold somewhere in its tree (``grade.matches``):
each key given must have that value; ``distance_m`` is a ``[low, high]``
range. Unset keys match anything.

query_hash.title: Query Hash
query_hash.description: sha256 of the canonical query object.

data_versions.title: Data Versions
data_versions.description: Dataset version of every layer the query touched.

ids_hash.title: Ids Hash
ids_hash.description: sha256 of the sorted feature ids.

ResultStamp.title: ResultStamp
ResultStamp.description:
A result without its features (design "Ergebnis-Stempel", F-8.9).

Same query on the same data gives the same stamp; comparing stamps tells
whether a saved result still holds, without storing the features.

RunCase.title: RunCase
RunCase.description:
A case as the run asked it (H7): the whole case, so the matrix, V7 and the
export read what it demanded here, not from the case store, which may have
changed since, and a run can be graded again.

RunLabel.title: RunLabel
RunLabel.description:
What a run measured against (F-3.18): without it a figure is worthless
after the next version change.

RunRequest.title: RunRequest
RunRequest.description:
A run as V4 composes it; the run keeps it (``RunView.request``), so
"Als vollständigen Lauf wiederholen" opens V4 with it.

query.description: The result query object, e.g. to count its hits.
The result query object, e.g. to count its hits.

data_changed.title: Data Changed
data_changed.description: A layer of the stamp has a new version or is gone (design C3 'Daten neu').

ids_hash.title: Ids Hash
ids_hash.description: sha256 of the sorted feature ids.

data_changed.title: Data Changed
data_changed.description: A layer of the stamp has a new version or is gone (design C3 'Daten neu').

query.description: The result query object; null without a result layer.

SessionWrite.title: SessionWrite
SessionWrite.description: What the interface saves: the whole analysis state and its result query.

SourceReason.title: SourceReason
SourceReason.description: The two sides' results are features of different layers.

StartPassword.title: StartPassword
StartPassword.description: Shown once to the administrator; the user must change it at first sign-in.

SystemStatus.title: SystemStatus
SystemStatus.description: What the instance runs on; for administrators only (security review #10).

TextMatch.title: TextMatch
TextMatch.description: Text search in a string attribute (F-4.2).

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.description: Sessions of any account that refer to this query.

ValueColumn-Input.title: ValueColumn
ValueColumn-Input.description:
Attribute ``attr`` of the feature of ``layer`` the result feature relates to.

Reads ``result <predicate> layer``. When several features qualify, the one
with the lowest ``fid`` gives the value; null when none does.

ValueColumn-Output.title: ValueColumn
ValueColumn-Output.description:
Attribute ``attr`` of the feature of ``layer`` the result feature relates to.

Reads ``result <predicate> layer``. When several features qualify, the one
with the lowest ``fid`` gives the value; null when none does.

ValueDomain.title: ValueDomain
ValueDomain.description: A range for numbers or a code list (code → meaning), F-2.8.

ValueMetric.title: ValueMetric
ValueMetric.description: Sum, mean, minimum or maximum of a numeric source attribute per area.
